problem: The lead says confusing scope with lifetime causes UnboundLocalError. UnboundLocalError actually comes from the compile-time rule that any name assigned anywhere in a function is local for the whole function, not from mixing up scope and lifetime.
fix: Confusing the two causes other errors; UnboundLocalError comes from a separate rule: any name assigned anywhere in a function is treated as local for the whole call, even before the assignment runs.

problem: "unless you use a mutable object, a module name, or a parameter" — a plain parameter does not carry a value from one call to the next. Only a default argument value, which is created once and reused, does that.
fix: unless you use a mutable default argument value, a module-level name, or an attribute on an object that outlives the call.

problem: "A local name lives from the moment the function call starts until the call returns" clashes with the bullet list below, which says print(x) finds x marked local but with no value yet. The name slot exists from the start; the binding happens only at the assignment.
fix: A local name is created in the function's frame when the call starts, but it is bound to an object only when its assignment runs. Both the name and the frame go away when the call returns.
